item.title: #3582969: Tool Explorer RC cleanup: render arrays, dead cache tag, menu placement, first tests
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +206/−33 · php +200/−28 · yml +4/−3 · md +2/−2
  • Diff: 4a70bb0
  • Discussion: #3582969 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

The Tool Explorer submodule now lives at /admin/config/development/tool-explorer, matching its place under Configuration > Development in the menu. The old /admin/config/tool/explorer path is gone, and the change landed before the RC1 URL freeze. The Extend page now shows a Configure link to the explorer. On the tool view page, YAML schema output containing < characters is now displayed correctly instead of being mangled, and the schema status messages use Drupal's standard status message markup.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Tool Explorer routes tool_explorer.list, tool_explorer.view and tool_explorer.execute moved from /admin/config/tool/explorer to /admin/config/development/tool-explorer.

Technical details

In ToolExplorerController, the hand-built #markup strings (<pre> YAML and messages--status/messages--warning divs) were replaced by two private static helpers. buildMessage() returns a #theme => status_messages element. buildYaml() returns an html_tag pre whose #value is Html::escape(Yaml::encode(...)). Escaping up front is needed because html_tag passes a plain #value through Xss::filterAdmin(), which strips anything resembling a tag. The tool_list cache tag was removed from the list table's #cache, since nothing invalidated it. The user.permissions context is kept. The three routes in tool_explorer.routing.yml changed path, and tool_explorer.info.yml gained configure: tool_explorer.list. Tests: the existing ToolExecuteFormTest paths were updated. A new ToolExplorerPagesTest covers anonymous 403, the list, the view page, YAML escaping, a 404 for unknown plugins, and the Extend page configure link. A new tool_test fixture, angle_bracket_label_tool, has <none> in an input label to exercise the escaping. README and docs references to the old path were updated.

Upgrade

Update bookmarks, docs, and any tests that use the old explorer URLs:

/admin/config/tool/explorer                       -> /admin/config/development/tool-explorer
/admin/config/tool/explorer/{plugin_id}           -> /admin/config/development/tool-explorer/{plugin_id}
/admin/config/tool/explorer/{plugin_id}/execute   -> /admin/config/development/tool-explorer/{plugin_id}/execute

Route names (tool_explorer.list, tool_explorer.view, tool_explorer.execute) are unchanged, so code that builds URLs from route names needs no change.

item.title: #3586821: Cache flush on VDB installation does not work
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +2/−0 · yml +2
  • Diff: 33ff73a
  • Discussion: #3586821 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Installing a module that alters Vector DB provider definitions now takes effect immediately. Before, the cached VDB provider plugin definitions were not cleared on module install, so the alter was missing until a manual cache rebuild. Config installed by that module could therefore run against the unaltered plugin class.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The ai.vdb_provider plugin manager is not named plugin.manager.*, so core's PluginManagerPass never tagged it plugin_manager_cache_clear. ai_modules_installed() clears ai_provider_plugins but not ai_vdb_provider_info_plugins. The commit adds tags: [{ name: plugin_manager_cache_clear }] to ai.vdb_provider in ai.services.yml. This clears the definitions cache before config install, which a hook_modules_installed() implementation cannot do. The issue also notes that a 1.x backport of #3535939 would help, but that is not part of this commit.

Upgrade

No action needed. Rebuild caches once after updating so the container picks up the new service tag.

item.title: #3586819: ChatFormBlock::blockAccess() passes NULL to load() when no AI Assistant is configured (array_flip() warning)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +10/−1 · php +10/−1
  • Diff: 2d95e74
  • Discussion: #3586819 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

An AI Chatbot block with no AI Assistant selected no longer triggers an array_flip() PHP warning in the log. This showed up on sites where a page builder or similar tool creates every block plugin with default configuration and checks access on each one. The unconfigured block is now simply treated as not accessible.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ChatFormBlock::blockAccess() passed $this->configuration['ai_assistant'] straight to the ai_assistant entity storage load(). With default configuration that value is empty, so EntityStorageBase::loadMultiple() received [NULL] and logged the warning. blockAccess() now reads the ID first and returns AccessResult::forbidden('No AI Assistant configured.') when it is not a non-empty string. Otherwise it loads the entity and runs the existing exists and enabled checks. This matches the guard already in ChatFormBlock::build() and the unconfigured handling in DeepChatFormBlock::blockAccess() (#3577813).

item.title: #3583114: Nullable inputs use two spellings in the generated JSON Schema
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +75/−19 · php +75/−19
  • Diff: a8945e9
  • Discussion: #3583114 · 1 contributor · 9 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Optional (nullable) tool inputs are now described in the generated JSON Schema with a single spelling: type: ["string", "null"], with format and similar keywords beside it. Before, optional strings, booleans and integers came out as oneOf: [{type: T}, {type: null}] on Drupal 11.1+, while optional date-time inputs used a type list, so clients that generate types from the schema saw two shapes for the same idea. The published schema for those inputs changes, so any client or test that matches the oneOf form needs updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Generated input JSON Schema for nullable scalars changes from oneOf: [{type: T}, {type: null}] to type: [T, "null"] on Drupal 11.1+.

Technical details

InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer gets a new protected method flattenNullableOneOf(), called on the schema returned by core's json_schema normalizer. It rewrites a oneOf into a type list only when every branch is a bare type string, one branch is null, and at most one branch carries extra keywords (such as format), which are moved beside the type. A oneOf with no null branch, with branches that say more than a type, or with two branches that carry their own keywords is left untouched. The type list replaces oneOf at its original key position, and existing sibling keys are not overwritten. The legacy path (pre-11.1 cores via LegacyTypedDataNormalizer) already emitted type lists, so both core paths now produce the same shape. InputSchemaMatrixTest and RicherSchemaEmissionTest drop their per-core oneOf expectations for nullable scalars.

Upgrade

Clients, schema snapshots or tests that expect the old nullable form must switch to the type list:

{"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}

becomes

{"type": ["string", "null"]}

item.title: #3583070: Config sequences keyed by name are derived as lists, so their schema says array while their values are objects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +906/−44 · php +821/−40 · md +50/−4 · yml +35
  • Diff: ab2d362
  • Discussion: #3583070 · 1 contributor · 19 comments

Summary

Tool definitions can now describe an object keyed by names that are not known in advance, such as an entity reference's target_bundles (bundle ID to bundle ID) or an image style's effects (keyed by UUID). Before, these config sequences were always derived as lists and published as a JSON array. Strict clients then rejected the object the setting needs, or sent a list that lost the names. A map-shaped value sent anyway was wrapped into a one-item list. Such maps are now published as a JSON object, each value is validated against the item type, and an empty map is sent as {}. Existing list derivations are unchanged unless a sequence is marked or named as keyed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: InputDefinition::fromConfigSchema() and fromDataDefinition() take a new optional $keyed_sequences argument; a sequence with orderby: key is now derived as a MapInputDefinition instead of a ListInputDefinition.
  • New API: MapInputDefinition and MapOutputDefinition accept an item_definition (with getItemDefinition(), setItemDefinition(), getItemValues() on MapDefinitionBase), published as additionalProperties.

Technical details

MapDefinitionBase gains an optional item definition, which describes every key the map does not declare. MapInputDefinition and MapOutputDefinition take it as a new last constructor argument, item_definition, and each enforces its own input or output interface. A map can declare properties and an item definition together: declared keys use their own definitions and all other keys use the item definition. The JSON schema normalizer (InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer) emits additionalProperties with the item schema. TypedInputsTrait and TypedOutputsTrait validate the undeclared keys against the item definition. RecursiveToolValueTransformSubscriber transforms each item. For outputs, a null in an optional item is dropped. A map whose keys run 0, 1, 2 is returned as an ArrayObject, so it is encoded as an object rather than a JSON array (#3583073).

In InputDefinition::fromDataDefinition(), a config sequence becomes a MapInputDefinition when it has orderby: key, or when the caller names its property path in the new $keyed_sequences argument. Otherwise it stays a ListInputDefinition. Paths use dots between property names, * for the items of a sequence, and an empty string for the definition itself. fromConfigSchema() takes the same argument. Config schema does not mark keyed sequences in general, so the caller has to name them.

Other changes: InputTypeCoercionSubscriber now treats a JSON string starting with an opening brace as a map even when its keys decode to a sequential array (object keys 0 and 1). OutputTypeCoercionSubscriber leaves a list-keyed map with an item definition to the recursive walk. OutputDefinition::fromContextDefinition() carries the item over. The refiner check in TypedInputsTrait applies the item-type narrowing rule to keyed maps. ToolInfoCommand prints an example_key example for such a map. The docs gain a "Maps keyed by name" section.

Upgrade

To declare a map keyed by name:

'target_bundles' => new MapInputDefinition(
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('Target bundles'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('The bundles to reference, keyed by bundle ID.'),
  item_definition: new InputDefinition(
    data_type: 'string',
    label: new TranslatableMarkup('Bundle'),
    description: new TranslatableMarkup('A bundle ID.'),
  ),
),

To derive keyed sequences from config schema, name them in the second argument:

$settings = InputDefinition::fromConfigSchema(
  ['type' => 'entity_reference_selection.default'],
  ['target_bundles'],
);

A refiner must not change the item data type of a list or keyed map (for example string to integer), or it throws a LogicException.

item.title: #3582977: Pass entities between drush tool:run calls as handles
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +1035/−89 · php +929/−72 · md +106/−17
  • Diff: dedbe8a
  • Discussion: #3582977 · 1 contributor · 39 comments

Summary

drush tool:run can now chain tools that work on content entities. An entity output prints as a handle:<uuid> string with a hint naming the entity, and a content entity input accepts that string, as the AI connector and MCP bridge already do. Every call in a chain must run with the same --uid, because handles are stored per account. The original proposal to hide such tools from CLI listings was not what shipped: they stay listed, and tool:list, tool:search and tool:info flag them with requires_handle.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: tool:run accepts and prints handle:<uuid> strings for content entities, --json output gains a hints list, and tool:list, tool:search and tool:info JSON gain requires_handle. EntityHandleTransformer gains hasContentEntityInputs(), hasRequiredContentEntityInputs() and hasContentEntityOutputs().

Technical details

DrushInvoker::create() now returns new Invoker(self::ID, InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles), so the existing handle transformer applies to drush runs. tool:run prints the formatted result: content entities as handles, plus a hints list under --json or a "Hints:" block in text output, shown only when there are hints.

EntityHandleTransformer gains hasContentEntityInputs(), hasRequiredContentEntityInputs() and hasContentEntityOutputs(). They recurse into list items and map properties through a private containsContentEntityDefinition(). requires_handle is true only when a required content entity input exists. A tool that only returns an entity, or whose entity input is optional, can be the first call of a chain. isConfigEntityDefinition() and isContentEntityDefinition() now strip a bundle suffix such as node:article before the entity type lookup, because getDefinition() throws a LogicException for such IDs.

tool:run logs a warning when run as uid 0 and the tool requires or returns a content entity. Anonymous tempstore owners do not persist across drush processes, so no handle reaches another call. The old "drush tool:run cannot pass entities" advice is replaced by entityInputAdvice(). It says "Pass the handle an earlier call returned." for content entity inputs and "Pass the machine name of the <type>." for config entity inputs, which take a machine name (#3583059). tool:info shows a "Requires handle" line and builds its example command with --uid=UID and HANDLE placeholders. It omits optional entity inputs and uses MACHINE_NAME for config entity inputs. The skill and drush docs were updated with a "Chain entity tools" section.

Upgrade

Tool authors need no changes. Scripts or agents that parse tool:list --format=json or tool:search output get a new boolean requires_handle on each tool. Handle chain example from the docs:

drush tool:run tool_belt:entity_stub --uid=7 --input=entity_type_id=node --input=bundle=article --json
drush tool:run tool_belt:field_set_value --uid=7 --json \
  --input='{"entity":"handle:…","field_name":"title","value":[{"value":"Hello"}]}'
drush tool:run tool_belt:entity_save --uid=7 --json --input=entity=handle:…

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 31, 2026
  • Committed: November 9, 2026 (3 months later)

item.title: #3601385: --config-url: accept a drupal.org project URL and translate it to the git.drupalcode.org repo URL
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +275/−5 · bats +184 · sh +85/−1 · md +3/−3 · 1 +2 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 5a37c56
  • Discussion: #3601385 · 1 contributor · 26 comments

Summary

--config-url now accepts a drupal.org project page URL such as https://www.drupal.org/project/ai and translates it to the matching https://git.drupalcode.org/project/ai repo before cloning. The installer prints a Resolved drupal.org project ... line showing what it will clone. Git URLs, SSH remotes, other hosts and non-project drupal.org pages are left untouched.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new helper, _normalize_config_url in src/lib/config/_normalize_config_url.sh, is called at the top of load_config_url() before the clone. Other loaders such as --config-path are unaffected. A remote-configs.json pointer that goes through follow_remote_config re-enters load_config_url, so it gets the same translation.

The helper matches http(s)://(www.|new.)?drupal.org/project/ case-insensitively on the host. It drops any query string or fragment, then splits the rest of the path on /. It skips drupal.org's own /project/ sections (issues, usage, releases, search), the browse listings (project_module, project_theme, project_theme_engine, project_distribution, project_core) and the modules/themes/distributions aliases. So /project/issues/ai and /project/ai/issues/12345 both resolve to ai. The first remaining segment is the machine name. If it is missing or doesn't match ^[a-z0-9_-]+$, the original URL is returned unchanged rather than inventing a repo URL. That means /project/AI, /project/issues and /docs/... all pass through. A lookalike host such as drupal.org.evil.com is not rewritten.

Bats tests were added for the normalizer (_normalize_config_url) and for the load_config_url clone. The --config-url help text, man page and AGENTS.md source-layout notes were updated.

Upgrade

Existing git URLs work unchanged. To use the new form, pass the project page URL directly:

--config-url https://www.drupal.org/project/ai

Contribution

  • Committed: November 9, 2026 (3 months later)

item.title: #3586706: Duplicate publishes the copy for users who may not use the publish transition
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +525/−109 · php +495/−98 · md +30/−11
  • Diff: 5403b87
  • Discussion: #3586706 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The Duplicate action on AI Context items now always creates a draft copy, for every user and whether or not "Publish by default" is on. Before, a user who could not use the Publish transition could still get a published copy, which skipped editorial review. The copy is also now owned by the user who duplicated it, gets new created and changed dates, and keeps neither the original's publishing schedule nor its revision log message. A user without the "Create new draft" transition now gets a form error instead of a copy. At the global item limit, duplicating a global item now saves a draft and shows no error, because the limit is checked when the copy is published. Sites running earlier versions should look for published items with the same label or created date as another item and review them.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Editorial workflow bypass: a user without the publish transition could get a published copy through Duplicate when Publish by default was on. Needs restricted permissions (Create and Edit AI Context Item).
  • Permission change: Duplicate now requires the use ai_context_editorial transition create_new_draft permission. Users without it get a form error, even if they may publish.

Technical details

The cause was in AiContextItemDuplicateForm::buildDuplicate(). It set the published status and the published moderation state from default_status, and validateForm() only ran the module persistence rules, never entity validation. So Content Moderation's ModerationState constraint never checked the transition. Now buildDuplicate() always produces a draft, using the new setDuplicateState() to call setUnpublished() and set moderation_state to draft on every translation. createDuplicate() copies all translations, but the route only passes the one in the current content language. validateForm() also calls ->validate() on the moderation_state field and turns each violation into a form error. A new item is checked as a transition from the workflow's initial state, so the user needs the Create new draft transition.

buildDuplicate() also resets fields that described the original. The RESET_FIELDS constant (uid, created, changed, publish_on, publish_state, unpublish_on, unpublish_state) gets applyDefaultValue() on each translation, since created and changed are translatable. The revision creation time and log message are reset through the entity type's revision metadata keys. The revision user is set to NULL so that AiContextItem::preSave() falls back to the owner. getDefaultStatus() and the config factory constructor argument are removed, and getDescription() always returns "A new draft copy will be created." The description of "Publish by default" in AiContextItemSettingsForm now says Duplicate always creates a draft. The docs are updated, including the removal of references to a "Duplicate tab". Kernel tests (AiContextItemDuplicateFormTest, new AiContextItemDuplicateScheduleTest) and functional tests in AiContextItemListTest were updated or added.

Upgrade

Grant use ai_context_editorial transition create_new_draft (AI Context editorial workflow: Use Create new draft transition) to any role that should keep using Duplicate. Copies made before this fix keep the original's label and created date, so check for published items sharing a label or created date with another item. This check also finds legitimate copies made by users who could publish.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 8, 2026
  • Committed: November 9, 2026

Key contributors

  • kristen pol (Itty Bitty Byte)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586703: Diff pages show older context item revisions without the revision permission
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +170/−5 · php +133 · md +37/−5
  • Diff: 10e82ec
  • Discussion: #3586703 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

When the Diff module was installed, any user who could use published AI context could open Diff comparison pages for context items and read older published revisions. That includes text editors had removed on purpose, and on sites that grant the permission to Anonymous, anonymous visitors. The Diff pages now need the same "View all AI Context Item revisions" permission as the revision history pages. Sites on Diff 8.x-1.x, 2.0.0 or 2.1.0 were affected. Diff 2.0.1 and 2.1.1 already require this upstream. After updating, review which roles have the revision permission and rebuild caches so the router picks up the new requirement.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Access bypass: on Diff 8.x-1.x, 2.0.0 and 2.1.0, users with only "Use Published AI Context in AI Features" (possibly Anonymous) could view older published revisions through Diff comparison pages. Priority major.
  • Permission change: Diff comparison pages for context items now require "View all AI Context Item revisions" (or Administer AI Context), plus view access to the item.

Technical details

AiContextRouteSubscriber::alterRoutes() now takes the route entity.ai_context_item.revisions_diff, if present, and sets _entity_access to ai_context_item.view all revisions. This is the requirement of the revision history route. Diff's controller still checks view access on each of the two revisions. The route also gets the no_cache option, because Diff adds no cache metadata for those per-revision checks. The option applies on Diff 2.0.1 and 2.1.1 too, because upstream does not set it there.

A new kernel test, AiContextItemRevisionDiffAccessTest::testDiffRouteNeedsRevisionPermission, checks that a user with only access published ai context is denied. It also checks that a user with view all ai context item revisions is allowed, and it asserts the route requirement and the no_cache option. require-dev stays on drupal/diff: ^1.0 so the test runs against a Diff version without the upstream change. Docs were updated in access-boundaries.md (a new "Revision and Diff pages" section), configuration.md and revisions.md.

Upgrade

Rebuild caches after updating (drush cr) so the router uses the new requirement. Grant View all AI Context Item revisions to any role that should still compare revisions with Diff.

  • Committed: November 9, 2026

item.title: #3586702: Usage records keep every request path with no limit on number or length
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +471/−30 · php +417/−27 · md +53/−3 · yml +1
  • Diff: fd64e41
  • Discussion: #3586702 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

With usage tracking on, a user who could send requests to a push consumer (for example a chatbot) could make a usage record grow without limit by sending a different, very long path in each request. That slowed AI requests for everyone using the consumer and could make them fail. Each usage record now keeps only the last 20 request paths, each at most 255 characters, and a client-supplied path hint longer than 2,048 characters is ignored. Errors from usage tracking during agent runs are now logged and no longer fail the run. Usage tracking is off by default. A record saved before the update is cut the next time a path is added to it. A record already too large to load is not cut and must be cleared.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Unbounded growth of usage record routes from client-supplied paths could slow or break AI requests of a push consumer for all users (denial of service, no data exposure); usage tracking is off by default.

Technical details

The new AiContextUsage::setRoutes() drops empty and non-string values, truncates each path to MAX_ROUTE_LENGTH (255) characters with Unicode::truncate() and an ellipsis, moves repeated paths to the end, and stores only the last MAX_ROUTES (20). addRoute() now delegates to it, so a repeated path moves to the end instead of keeping its first position. In AiContextUsageTracker::attachEntity(), the old record's routes are merged first (setRoutes(array_merge(old, current))), so the limit drops the oldest paths and keeps the run's. A new record for another entity gets its first path through addRoute(), so the limits apply there too.

AiContextRequestInfoResolver::normalizeSuppliedPath() returns NULL when the path, after the query string and fragment are removed, is longer than MAX_PATH_LENGTH (2048) characters (mb_strlen()). setPath() then returns FALSE and getPath() falls through to the next source, ending at the request path, which has no limit of its own.

AiContextAgentToolSubscriber::onToolFinished() wraps recordToolUsed(), extractEntityInfo() and attachEntity() in a try block. AiContextAgentFinishedSubscriber::onAgentFinished() does the same for flushToolsUsed(). Both catch Throwable and log an error naming the runner ID. AiContextAgentFinishedSubscriber gets a LoggerInterface as its second constructor argument, wired to @logger.channel.ai_context in ai_context.services.yml. A PHP memory-limit error is fatal and is not a Throwable, so the path limits are the main fix and the try/catch is a second safeguard. No update hook is added. All changed classes are @internal.

Upgrade

If a consumer already fails because of oversized usage records, turn off usage tracking at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/usage, then clear the records at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/usage/clear. If the clear page also fails, empty the table and rebuild the caches:

drush sql:query "TRUNCATE TABLE ai_context_usage"
drush cr

item.title: #3586701: Core "view any unpublished content" permission shows unpublished context items
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +217/−9 · php +174/−9 · md +43
  • Diff: 94b0dbc
  • Discussion: #3586701 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

Users whose role had core's "View any unpublished content" permission, such as the Content editor role on Drupal CMS, could read draft and archived AI Context items even with no AI Context permission. This included the item page, the Latest version tab, revision pages, and the CCC listing for roles that also had "View AI Context Items in CCC". After the fix, unpublished items are visible only to users with "Administer AI Context", "View any unpublished AI Context Item", or the owner holding "View AI Context Items in CCC". Roles that need to see drafts must be given "View any unpublished AI Context Item". Published items are unchanged. Run drush cr after updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

The revision history and revision pages need the revision permission plus view access to each revision. Docs were updated in access-boundaries.md, configuration.md and api-stability.md.

Items are actually injected as a block with an ID, label and purpose header and indented guidance. Items that looked like they fit within Max tokens for injection could still be cut off at render time. The "Items cut off due to token limit: 4" warning also now says what the number means: how many of the selected items did not fit, which token budget, which consumer, and the item IDs. After updating, run drush updatedb and drush cr. Expect higher badges, percentages and budget totals. Sites near their budget may now see Context budget exceeded. Selection and rendering behave as before.

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: Update 10032 recounts the stored token_count of every ai_context_item revision and translation so it covers the rendered block.
  • Config change: No config schema change; the consumer budget summary note and the cut-off warning text are reworded.

A new item has no ID in preSave(), so postSave() recounts it and writes the result through the new AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler::writeTokenCounts(). The scheduler now takes @ai_context.renderer as a constructor argument.

drush cr

item.title: #3586645: Usage records and the invocation result count items that the token budget left out
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +655/−45 · php +604/−34 · md +51/−11
  • Diff: 4b0d01f
  • Discussion: #3586645 · 1 contributor · 25 comments

Summary

When a consumer's token budget is too small, the renderer shortens some context items and leaves others out. Before this fix, usage records and the generic-path invocation result still counted every selected item as delivered. The usage pages could then show an item as used by a consumer whose prompt never contained it. Now only items that reached the prompt are recorded and reported. A shortened item still counts as delivered, because part of it reached the model. An item the budget left out does not count.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Generic-path invocation result item_ids and item_count now contain only delivered items, so they can be smaller than the selection on sites with a tight token budget.
  • New API: AiContextSelectionResult::getOmittedItemIds() and getDeliveredItemIds(), plus AiContextSelectionTextRenderedEvent::getOmittedItemIds(), and an omitted_item_ids key in the renderer result.

Technical details

AiContextRenderer::render() now returns an omitted_item_ids list next to truncated_item_ids. It holds the IDs that produced no block at all: the budget had no room, or the entity could not be loaded or was unpublished. getTruncatedItemIds() is unchanged and still covers both shortened and dropped items, so an ID can appear in both lists. AiContextSelector passes the list into AiContextSelectionTextRenderedEvent (read-only, new trailing constructor argument omittedItemIds) and into AiContextSelectionResult.

AiContextSelectionResult::getDeliveredItemIds() returns getSelectedItemIds() minus the omitted IDs. AiContextBuildSystemPromptSubscriber (agent path) and AiContextPreGenerateResponseSubscriber (generic path) use it for recordUsage(). The generic path also uses it for the invocation result. getSelectedItemIds() is unchanged. The renderer decides what counts as delivered, so a TEXT_RENDERED subscriber that edits item text does not change the records.

The generic path still decides whether to push based on the selection, not on delivered items. If the budget leaves out every selected item but a TEXT_RENDERED subscriber added text, that text is pushed with status pushed, empty item_ids and item_count 0. In that case no usage is recorded. The docs (api-stability.md, consumer_api.md, usage_tracking.md) are updated, with a new "Beta upgrade: usage and item_ids count delivered items" section. A new kernel test covers both push paths, using a length-based test tokenizer so budgets can actually be exceeded.

Upgrade

Code that compared item_count or item_ids in the invocation result against its own selection count may now see fewer items. Use getSelectedItemIds() for what selection chose and getDeliveredItemIds() for what reached the prompt:

$result->getSelectedItemIds();   // unchanged
$result->getOmittedItemIds();    // left out completely
$result->getDeliveredItemIds();  // selected minus omitted

item.title: #3586661: Saving or rendering context items fails when the tiktoken vocab cannot be loaded
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 20 files, +2210/−63 · php +1953/−59 · md +237/−4 · json +15 · yml +5
  • Diff: f05a82c
  • Discussion: #3586661 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

AI Context no longer breaks when the tokenizer cannot load its vocabulary file. That file is downloaded on first use from openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net and cached in the Drupal temp directory. Before this fix, a blocked download, a non-writable temp directory or a corrupt cache file made item saves fail with "The changes could not be saved." It also stopped agent tools that load context. Now AI Context uses an approximate token count (bytes divided by 4), logs one warning, and keeps saving items, rendering context and answering agent requests. Stored counts are recalculated by cron once the vocabulary loads. Sites without outbound access can allow the host or copy the vocab file into the temp directory. The new docs describe both options.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AiContextTokenEstimator::isTokenizerAvailable(), markTokenizerUnavailable() and reportEncodingFailure(), and AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler::queueDeferredRecount() and deferRecount().

Technical details

AiContextTokenEstimator::estimate() now catches \Throwable from setModel() and countTokens(). On failure it returns (int) ceil(strlen($text) / 4). The failure is remembered per model for UNAVAILABLE_CACHE_TTL (600 seconds), both in the service and in cache.default under ai_context:tokenizer_unavailable:{model}. Requests therefore do not retry the download, and drush cr clears the memo. One warning is logged per request to the ai_context channel. A text that fails to encode while the vocab is loaded gets an approximate count for that text only, and the tokenizer is not marked unavailable. The AI module's own cl100k_base fallback in Tokenizer::setModel() is uncaught, so the catch has to live in AI Context.

AiContextRenderer skips configureTextChunkerModel() when the tokenizer is unavailable and trims content with mb_strcut($content, 0, $max_tokens * 4) instead of TextChunker::chunkText(). It uses the same fallback if the chunker throws mid-render. While approximate counts are in use, the render result gets a max-age of 600 seconds, so cached output does not keep the byte-trimmed text after the vocab loads.

Fallback counts must not stay in storage permanently. AiContextItem::preSave() stores the approximate count and calls queueDeferredRecount(), which queues one full recount on ai_context_token_count_backfill. A state flag, ai_context.token_count_deferred_recount, limits this to one waiting recount. backfillChunk() checks isTokenizerAvailable() before counting and again before writing. When the tokenizer is unavailable it throws the @internal AiContextTokenizerUnavailableException and writes nothing. The queue worker turns that into SuspendQueueException. processQueuedChunk() releases the item and returns deferred: TRUE, and the settings-form batch shows a warning. backfillAll() and update 10023 call deferRecount() and finish instead of failing. Docs (services.md, configuration.md, debugging.md) were extended, and the kernel test base gained stubFailingTokenizerServices() with AiContextFailingTestTokenizer.

Upgrade

Sites that cannot reach the vocab host have two options. Allow outbound HTTPS to openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net, or copy the vocab file unchanged into the Drupal temp directory under the SHA-1 of its URL. The file for cl100k_base, which gpt-4 and unknown models use, is 9b5ad71b2ce5302211f9c61530b329a4922fc6a4. The file for o200k_base, used by gpt-4o models, is fb374d419588a4632f3f557e76b4b70aebbca790. Sites whose temp directory is emptied on each deploy can set $settings['file_temp_path'] to a persistent directory. After fixing the cause, run drush cr and then cron, so the approximate counts are recalculated.

item.title: #3586620: Context items listing replaces its cache metadata instead of merging it
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +107/−7 · php +107/−7
  • Diff: 6d8826d
  • Discussion: #3586620 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

The AI Context items listing page now keeps all of its cache metadata. Before, parts of it were overwritten, so the list cache tag and the per-user cache contexts were dropped. On a default site this changes nothing, because admin routes are not stored in Dynamic Page Cache. It matters only if a site or later change makes this page cacheable. In that case, a new item might not show until caches were cleared, and on older Drupal core versions another user could be served the owner's Draft rows.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

AiContextItemListBuilder used CacheableMetadata::applyTo(), which assigns #cache instead of merging it. In render(), the settings config metadata overwrote the ai_context_item_list tag that core's EntityListBuilder::render() puts on $build['table']. The view-access metadata (listAccessCacheability) was then overwritten by scopeLabelCacheability, so the user context and the tags of hidden items were lost. The same pattern was in the settings-access code and in the tooltip helper that writes #cache on the child label cell.

Each call site now starts from CacheableMetadata::createFromRenderArray($build) (or $build['table']), adds the extra metadata with addCacheableDependency(), and applies the result once. Two kernel tests were added: testTableKeepsTheCoreListCacheTag and testViewAccessAndScopeLabelMetadataBothSurvive.
